deviations: Bandwidth sample taken as |dif| <= 45 (inclusive), where dif = months between birth month-year and December 1955 (dif >= 0 is treated); the paper's equation writes an open interval, which was read as 'born within 45 months'.

Anderson (2008) indices built on respondents with all 20 SRQ-20 items answered: items standardized with the control-group (born Jan 1956 or later, full 72-month survey sample) mean and SD, weighted by row sums of the inverse covariance matrix of the standardized items (full sample), and the final index re-standardized to mean 0 / SD 1 in the control group.
notes: attempt-1: exploratory variable listing (no RESULT lines). attempt-2: first full estimation; fixest dropped 15-16 fixed-effect singleton observations by default, which changes N but not coefficients. Final run sets fixef.rm='none' so every respondent with outcome and controls observed is counted (as Stata reg/areg with dummies would); coefficients identical, SEs and N slightly different. This change was based on the paper's sample definition, not on any reported value. Specification: feols(y ~ before1955 + dif + dif*before1955 + i(education) + i(ethnicity) + female | birth month + province + surveyor), uniform kernel, SEs clustered by month-year of birth. Non-respondents (no birth date) excluded. No runs hung.
